key_insight: Introduce a shared low-rank LoRA subspace that captures and reuses task knowledge, enabling near-strict continual learning without task-specific adapters or data replay. This consolidates new tasks into a compact, extensible parameter subspace that prevents catastrophic forgetting.
problem_solved: How to adapt large pretrained models to a stream of new tasks efficiently and continually while avoiding catastrophic forgetting, high retraining costs, and the proliferation of separate adapters or replay buffers.
method: Learn a shared low-rank LoRA subspace (basis) across tasks so new tasks are represented by lightweight coefficient vectors rather than full adapters.
Incrementally update and expand the subspace only when necessary, with orthogonalization/regularization to preserve previously encoded directions and prevent forgetting.
Train task-specific coefficients in the shared subspace (few parameters), enabling strict continual updates without access to past data or multiple adapter copies.
impact: Drastically reduces storage and compute overhead for continual adaptation of large models while preserving past task performance, making deployment of continually updated models practical for production systems and hardware-constrained environments.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: pretrained model + shared LoRA subspace module with per-task coefficient vectors.
Process flow: sequential task arrival → coefficient update → conditional subspace expansion (illustrate orthogonalization/regularization).
Performance chart: accuracy vs. task index comparing Share vs. baseline LoRA, full fine-tuning, and replay (highlight reduced forgetting).
Resource bar graph: parameters/storage and compute for Share versus multiple adapters and replay-based methods.
paper_title: Shared LoRA Subspaces for almost Strict Continual Learning
paper_authors: Prakhar Kaushik, Ankit Vaidya, Shravan Chaudhari, Rama Chellappa, Alan Yuille
